subject: Learning Methods
title: ELI5: Explain Like I'm Five
description: A micro-lesson that makes ELI5: Explain Like I'm Five usable.

hook.text: The internet forum 'Explain Like I'm Five' forces contributors to strip complex topics to their bare essence.

buildup.text: Extreme simplification requires you to identify the one core idea and remove everything else.

discovery.text: The exercise reveals what actually matters. When you can say it in one sentence a child understands, you found the core.

twist.text: Simplification is not dumbing down. It is finding the real signal beneath layers of complexity and jargon.

climax.text: Try it: take any concept you're studying and explain it in one sentence a five-year-old could follow. That is mastery.

punchline.text: If a child can't follow your sentence, simplify further.

quiz.question: What does extreme simplification reveal about your understanding?
options: How much detail you can memorize
Whether you've identified the one core idea beneath the complexity
How many synonyms you know for technical terms
